steps.title: Why prepare OrderDetails_2 first?
steps.change: OrderDetails supplies every detail line because each line contributes quantity. Grouping by OrderID makes one CTE row per order; Orders supplies the outer report’s starting rows.
steps.added_sql:
WITH OrderDetails_2 AS (
    SELECT OrderID, SUM(Quantity) AS total_units
    FROM OrderDetails
    GROUP BY OrderID
)
SELECT OrderID, total_units
FROM OrderDetails_2
ORDER BY OrderID;

steps.title: Why start the outer query with Orders?
steps.change: The report counts orders and adds their amounts. Orders supplies one row per order and both IDs needed for the later lookups.
steps.added_sql: SELECT OrderID, ShipperID, Total_Order_Amount FROM Orders ORDER BY OrderID;
steps.sql: SELECT OrderID, ShipperID, Total_Order_Amount FROM Orders ORDER BY OrderID;

steps.title: Why add Shippers with a LEFT JOIN?
steps.change: Orders already carries ShipperID. Add Shippers second to look up its company name. Every order stays on the left, including an order with an unrecognised shipper ID.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT o.OrderID, o.ShipperID AS ordering_shipper_id, o.Total_Order_Amount,
       s.ShipperID AS matched_shipper_id, s.CompanyName
FROM Orders AS o
LEFT JOIN Shippers AS s
    ON o.ShipperID = s.ShipperID
ORDER BY o.OrderID;
steps.sql:

       s.ShipperID AS matched_shipper_id, s.CompanyName
FROM Orders AS o
LEFT JOIN Shippers AS s
    ON o.ShipperID = s.ShipperID
ORDER BY o.OrderID;

steps.title: Why LEFT JOIN the units summary third?
steps.change: The outer query already has `Orders.OrderID`, so it can attach the prepared `OrderDetails_2` total with a `LEFT JOIN` on `od.OrderID = o.OrderID`. The CTE contributes at most one units row per order; order 10 matches its two lines (2 + 3 = 5). Because this lookup is independent of the `Shippers` lookup—both keys come directly from `Orders`—either join can come first. A missing summary (like the separate OtherShip check for order 16) leaves the order and its amount 80 in place, with units NULL until `COALESCE` makes it 0.
steps.added_sql:
WITH OrderDetails_2 AS (
    SELECT OrderID, SUM(Quantity) AS total_units
    FROM OrderDetails
    GROUP BY OrderID
)
-- …
       s.ShipperID AS matched_shipper_id, s.CompanyName,
       od.OrderID AS summarized_order_id, od.total_units
-- …
LEFT JOIN `OrderDetails_2` AS od
    ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
steps.sql:
WITH OrderDetails_2 AS (
    SELECT OrderID, SUM(Quantity) AS total_units
    FROM OrderDetails
    GROUP BY OrderID
)
SELECT o.OrderID, o.ShipperID AS ordering_shipper_id, o.Total_Order_Amount,
       s.ShipperID AS matched_shipper_id, s.CompanyName,
       od.OrderID AS summarized_order_id, od.total_units
FROM Orders AS o
LEFT JOIN Shippers AS s
    ON o.ShipperID = s.ShipperID
LEFT JOIN `OrderDetails_2` AS od
    ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
ORDER BY o.OrderID;

steps.title: Why use the displayed shipper name for grouping?
steps.change: Each order contributes to one reporting label. COALESCE gives an unmatched lookup the label Unknown shipper so missing and unrecognised IDs feed the same group.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT COALESCE(s.CompanyName, 'Unknown shipper') AS shipper_name,
       o.OrderID, o.Total_Order_Amount, od.total_units
-- …
ORDER BY shipper_name, o.OrderID;
steps.sql:
WITH OrderDetails_2 AS (
    SELECT OrderID, SUM(Quantity) AS total_units
    FROM OrderDetails
    GROUP BY OrderID
)
SELECT COALESCE(s.CompanyName, 'Unknown shipper') AS shipper_name,
       o.OrderID, o.Total_Order_Amount, od.total_units
FROM Orders AS o
LEFT JOIN Shippers AS s
    ON o.ShipperID = s.ShipperID
LEFT JOIN `OrderDetails_2` AS od
    ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
ORDER BY shipper_name, o.OrderID;

steps.title: Why count, add and then sort?
steps.change: Count the order IDs, add each order amount once and add its units total. COALESCE turns a group’s all-NULL units total into zero. Sort the shipper totals by order value, highest first.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT
    COALESCE(s.CompanyName, 'Unknown shipper') AS shipper_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.OrderID) AS orders,
    SUM(o.Total_Order_Amount) AS order_value,
    COALESCE(SUM(od.total_units), 0) AS units_shipped
-- …
GROUP BY shipper_name
ORDER BY order_value DESC;
